title: Foot-in-the-Door as Social Engineering Formalization: Quantifying Commitment-Consistency Exploits

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: systematizing all six Cialdini principles as multi-turn attack vectors gives a principled taxonomy for threat modeling. Comparing compliance escalation rates across principles identifies which social dynamics safety training must address. Directly actionable for defense design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating 5 prompt sequences for each of 6 principles requires understanding social psychology literature and translating it into conversational manipulation tactics. Multi-turn API calls add some complexity. Feasible with mentor guidance but requires careful scenario design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Six principles times 5 sequences each is 30 multi-turn conversations to design and run. Plus measuring compliance escalation across turns for each. Moderate scope -- achievable in 30 hours if kept to 2-3 principles, but as stated covers all six.

novelty.reasoning: 'Foot-In-The-Door: A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs' was published at EMNLP 2025 (arXiv:2502.19820). This paper directly implements the foot-in-the-door technique as a multi-turn jailbreak, using SSParaphrase to progressively escalate malicious intent through intermediate bridge prompts. It achieves 94% average attack success rate across seven models, including 93%/90% on GPT-4o. MTSA (ACL 2025) provides multi-turn safety alignment as defense. The proposed idea — formalizing Cialdini's commitment-consistency principle as a multi-turn attack and measuring compliance escalation — is the exact contribution of this published EMNLP 2025 paper.
